newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs up $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs up $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs sold Thursday at prices $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt higher as producers shut down hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
"This is the worst I've ever seen, everybody just shut down at once," one central Iowa packer buyer said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog prices were up $0.50 to $1.00 at $51.50 to $52.00 in the country and $52.50 to $53.50 at plants.
Illinois hogs sold up $0.50 to $1.00 at $52.00-$52.50 in the country and $53.00-$53.50 at plants, with talk of non-reported plant sales $54.00-$54.50, some dealers said.

Indiana hog prices were up $1.00 amid light movement, with sales reported at $49.00 to $50.00 in the country and $51.00 to $52.00 at plants. Ohio dealers said hogs there sold up $0.50 to $1.00 at $49.00 to $50.00 in the country and $51.00 to $52.50 at plants.

Producers reportedly slowed marketings in response to steep price declines early this week, sources said. Those declines were linked to brisk marketings of hogs that were backlogged by last week's cold, snowy weather.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog runs Wednesday totaled 90,000 head, well below USDA's estimate of 105,000.
